$comment: US-590: THE single source of truth for ingredient-line parsing behaviour.
EatPal parses ingredient lines on two platforms — src/lib/parse-grocery-text.ts
on web, and ios/EatPal/Shared/IngredientTextParser.swift on iOS (which the
voice / paste / share-sheet path delegates to). They drifted badly enough that
the same paste produced different quantities, so both test suites now load
THIS file and must agree on every case:
Add a case here, not to one suite. `was` records the pre-audit output so a
regression is legible; it is documentation, not an assertion.
Name comparison is case-insensitive: the web parser preserves the input's
casing while the iOS grocery path title-cases for display.

cases.name: chicken thighs
cases.was: web: name "-3 lbs chicken thighs", qty 2, unit "" — range unparsed

cases.name: sugar
cases.note: mixed number SUMS; only a real range averages

cases.name: tomatoes
cases.was: web: 14.5 oz package size silently discarded; iOS: name began "(14.5"

cases.name: black beans
cases.note: hyphenated size descriptor, NOT a range endpoint (must not average to 8)

cases.name: garlic
cases.was: web: name "cloves garlic, minced", unit ""; iOS: emitted a phantom item "Minced"

cases.name: lettuce
cases.was: web + iOS: name "of lettuce" — the connective survived

cases.name: eggs
cases.was: web: qty 1, unit "", name "a dozen eggs" — word numbers unsupported

cases.name: milk
cases.was: web: name "a cup of milk" — the article survived

cases.name: ground beef
cases.note: "ground" is deliberately NOT a filler — stripping it yields "beef"

cases.name: avocados
cases.was: web emitted "ct" while iOS wrote "count"; iOS had no ct entry at all

cases.name: milk
cases.note: "gallon" canonicalises to "gal" so it matches the pantry defaults

cases.name: 2% milk
cases.note: a percentage is a product descriptor, not a quantity — must not parse as qty 2 with the name "% milk"

cases.name: half and half
cases.note: compound product name; a bare " and " must not split it
